set.rappels: 6 bolted rappels on a single 60 m rope (a 70 m is more comfortable) down the West Face
set.rappel_count_note: The bolted West Face line is the one-rope descent: six bolted stations in a nearly direct line back to the base. A single 60 m rope only just reaches on the tightest station, and a 70 m rope removes the squeeze. The start is about 15 ft right of where the final jam cracks end. After the last rappel into a chossy alcove, look skier's left around the corner for the final anchor, an easy walk. The older line off the south side goes through the notch and the chockstone; no source gives the length of the free-hanging rappel past the chockstone, so it is not listed here.
set.descent_text:
Two established ways off the summit; both are widely used and either works, but they return you to different spots relative to a gear stash at the base.

Bolted West Face rappel line (most direct back to packs at the base of NW Corner/West Face): from the summit, downclimb/walk skier's-left to the top of a clean, purpose-bolted rappel line down the right side of the West Face. Six bolted (2-bolt) rappel stations in a nearly direct line bring you back down to essentially the same spot where you left your pack at the base of the route. Pulls are reported as clean and the line is efficient — regulars find it a breeze. A single 60m rope is just barely sufficient (one station, reportedly the 3rd rappel, is tight enough that you may need to reach down to clip your PAS/daisy to the anchor and feed rope through your device to reach it); a 70m rope removes that squeeze and is the more comfortable choice. No natural anchors needed on this line — it's fully bolted.

Classic notch/chockstone descent (South/Southwest Gully): downclimb and rappel the south side into the notch separating North and South Early Winters Spire, then continue down the Southwest Gully (the South Early Winter Spire "Chockstone Route" descent). This runs three single-rope rappels from near the summit down to the notch/gully (which often holds snow even in summer), followed by one spectacular, largely free-hanging rappel down and past a huge chockstone (~50 ft of air), then a final short rappel (~30 ft, off a tree anchor) or downclimb/scramble to reach the base. Total is about 4-5 rappels on this line. Anchors are natural/fixed slings around the chockstone and trees rather than bolts — inspect webbing before trusting it. Summit-to-base time on this descent is typically around 1.5-2 hours. This option is the standard descent if you climbed a route on the south/southwest side, or as a backup if the West Face bolt line is congested or iced.

review.single_rope: Bolted West Face line is six single-rope stations; 60 m barely reaches, 70 m recommended. Classic line has three single-rope raps to the notch, then a free-hanging rap past the chockstone whose length no source gives.
review.changed: Replaced the classic-line table (which held a two-rope station) with the six-station bolted West Face line; removed two-rope wording from rappels, note and descent text.

set.rappels: Rappel the route on existing slung and natural anchors (trees, roots, blocks); a single 70 m rope has been used, so carry extra webbing and cord.
set.rappel_count_note: Parties report about 4-5 rappels on slung trees, roots and blocks, many with old slings; some anchors are brush cinched with webbing and one bolt has been damaged by rockfall. A single 70 m rope has been used for the descent, but the line is less obvious that way: after the first rappel, look climber's left for the next anchor, which is easy to miss. No station-by-station list with lengths is published, so none is shown. Inspect and back up worn anchors with extra webbing and rap rings.

review.single_rope: A single 70 m rope is reported as workable but not intuitive; count about 4-5; no station list or lengths published.

set.rappels: 4 rappels down the West Face, about 50 m, 50 m, 50 m and 20 m; one 60 m rope does not reach the first three
set.rappel_count_note: The published descent is four rappels of roughly 50 m, 50 m, 50 m and a short 20 m, down the north-ridge line to the packs at the base of the route. One 60 m rope reaches only about 30 m per rappel, so it does not cover the first three, and no intermediate station is known. The anchors are natural features with tat (flake, horn); parties reinforce them.
set.descent_text: Rappel down the center of the West Face; the published rappels are roughly 50 m, 50 m, 50 m and 20 m, which one rope does not reach for the first three, and no intermediate anchors are documented. The line uses natural anchor features and existing bolt/gear anchors established on the granite. Ensure proper rope management to avoid tangling on the steep granite face. Once back at the base of the route, climb back up to the Chikamin-Dome Col via the Chickamin Glacier approach, watching carefully for crevasses and potential moat crossings. From the col, descend the cross-country route back to Bachelor Flats (taking approximately 8-10 hours depending on snow coverage and conditions). From Bachelor Flats, follow the Downey Creek trail back to the trailhead (6-8 hours depending on fitness and pack weight). Plan on getting back to the col the day you climb, then two days out to the car.

review.single_rope: No single-rope descent is documented; the published rappels are about 50 m each, beyond one rope's reach.
review.changed: Cleared the table of 50 m stations, restated the count and lengths in single-rope terms, rewrote the one descent sentence that named the rope setup.

set.rappels: 3 rappels: 2 on a single 60 m rope off the summit tower, then a long one of about 60 m from the ridge saddle to the Redoubt Glacier that one rope does not reach
set.rappel_count_note: The full descent is three rappels: two single-rope rappels to the wide ledge, then from the saddle one long rappel of about 60 m off the highest anchor to the glacier below. One 60 m rope does not reach from the saddle to the glacier, and no intermediate station is known. Another party reported one single and one longer rappel with a 60 m rope from the summit to the base on a different line.
set.descent_text: Downclimb/reverse the ridge to the headwall, then rappel: parties commonly make several rappels down to the ridge's low point followed by a long rappel of about 60 m back onto Redoubt Glacier that one rope does not reach, then reverse the approach to camp.

rappel_detail.notes: First of two single-rope rappels descending the ridge toward its low point.
Second single-rope rappel continuing down to the ridge's low point. Below here, one rope does not reach the glacier; no shorter line is documented.

review.single_rope: Two single-rope rappels to the saddle; the long final rappel to the glacier is about 60 m and has no documented single-rope version.
review.changed: Dropped the 60 m station from the table, kept the two single-rope stations, and restated the last section plainly in single-rope terms.

set.rappels: 3 rappels if you traverse in, 4 if you top out; long full-rope lines that one rope does not cover
set.rappel_count_note: The published descent is 3 rappels if you traverse in, or 4 if you top out, each a long full-length line from fixed anchors, trending left tree to tree. One 60 m rope reaches about 30 m per rappel, and no intermediate anchors are documented, so a one-rope descent is not described. Inspect the fixed slings before use; damage from pikas has been reported at the anchors. The alternative is the scree slope, with the rope as a handline.
set.descent_text: From the top of the wall, long rappels from tree anchors on climber's left lead back down, trending slightly left to the next ledge — inspect any fixed gear before trusting it due to reported pika damage at anchors. Alternatively, descend the scree slope, using the full rope length as a handline/backup if downclimbing.

review.single_rope: No single-rope descent documented; sources give 3-4 long rappels and no lengths.
review.changed: Removed the two-rope wording, gave the 3-4 count, stated plainly that one rope is not documented; kept the tree anchors, pika damage and scree alternative from the existing row.

set.rappels: About 3 rappels: eastward down the gully to the Pernod-Chablis notch, followed by two or so more down steep slabs to the neve; none documented for a single rope
set.rappel_count_note: The descent is a rappel eastward down the gully to the Pernod-Chablis notch, followed by two or so more down steep slabs to the neve below. No per-rappel lengths are published, no single-rope line is documented, and no intermediate anchors are known. The only fixed rappel anchor on the route is on the summit ridge, where nuts were left; the slab anchors are natural and unreliable.
set.descent_text: From the top of the Direct West Face, rappel east down the gully to the Pernod-Chablis notch (rappel 1), then make a couple more rappels down steep slabs to the neve/snowfield below (rappels 2 and 3) — three rappels total to get off the technical ground. No single-rope line is documented for these. The only fixed rappel anchor on the route is on the summit ridge, where nuts have been left in place; everything else, including the old aid bolts used to reach the summit block (one reported missing a hanger, another loose in its hole), should be treated as unreliable — back up or build natural gear anchors in cracks/horns where you can. From the neve, trend north around the base of Chianti Spire and climb back up to Burgundy Col (~7,770 ft), then descend the climbers' path down the scree gullies to the bench camp and boot path back to the highway pullout. Budget real time for this — the three raps only get you to the neve, after which there's a substantial re-ascent to the col before the walk-off begins.

review.single_rope: Nothing documented for one rope; no lengths published.

set.rappels: Several: from the summit back to the Pernod-Chianti notch, then long rappels down the east side to the glacier edge (no published count or single-rope line)
set.rappel_count_note: No published count: rappels lead from the summit back to the notch between Pernod and Chianti, then long rappels descend the east side to the glacier edge. They are described as long, and no single-rope line or intermediate anchors are documented.
set.descent_text: This is a rappel descent, not a walk-off. Rappel from the summit block back to the notch between Pernod and Chianti, then make long rappels down the east side to the snow and névé at the edge of the Silver Star Glacier basin. No rappel count is published for this line; carry cord to back up or replace old slings and bolts. From the glacier edge, traverse back north below Chianti and climb a few hundred feet to regain Burgundy Col, then descend the climbers' trail (scree, the bench, then the timbered rib) to the SR-20 pullout. Watch for moats along the rock late in the season, and budget real time for the loose scree below the col.
